senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; כהן , v. כּוּן; cmp. b. h. כַּן) [standing, stationed,] officer, esp. priest.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 6a:4">Yoma 6ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כ׳ גדול</he> (abbr. <he>כ״ג</he>) high priest, <he>כ׳ הדיוט</he> ordinary priest.

<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 1:9">Meg. I, 9</cite> <he>כ׳ משוח</he> an anointed high priest, contrad. to <he>מרובה בגדים</he> a high priest distinguished only by his robes (but not anointed, as in the days of the Second Temple).
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 1:9">Ib.</cite> <he>כ׳ משמש</he> officiating highpriest, <he>כ׳ שעבר</he> a substitute of the high priest no longer required, ex-substitute.

<cite ref="Mishnah Horayot 3:8">Hor. III, 8</cite> <he>ממזר … קודם לכ״ג ע״ה</he> a bastard who is a scholar has the precedence of an ignorant high priest; a. v. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="K00168"><he>כֹּהֲנִים</he></cite>.
Yeb. 86ᵇ, a. e. בכ״ד מקומות נקראו הכ׳ וכ׳ in twenty four Biblical passages the priests are designated as Levites; a. v. fr.—תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים (abbr. ת״כ) Torath Kohănim,

senses.gloss: name of the third book of Moses, Leviticus.
units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 7:3">Lev. R. s. 7</cite> <he>מפני מה … בת״כ</he> why do we, in teaching children, commence with Leviticus? a. e.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: name of an halachic commentary to Leviticus, also named Sifra.
units: Yeb. 72ᵇ; a. fr.—Fem. כֹּהֶנֶת, כּוֹהֶ׳ a priest’s daughter or wife.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 4:8">Keth. IV, 8</cite> <he>ובכ׳</he> and in the case of a priest’s wife.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 7:1">Ib. VII, 1</cite>, sq. (70ᵃ) <he>ובכ׳</he> Mish. a. Y. ed. (Bab. ed. <he>ובכהן</he>). Ib. 71ᵃ; a. fr.—Pl. <he>כֹּהֲנוֹת</he>, <he>כּוֹהֲ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 3:10">Yeb. III, 10</cite> <he>אם היו כ׳</he> (Y. ed. <he>כוה׳</he>) if they are daughters of priests; a. e.
